A defensible protocol, synthesized from evaluation and feature-ablation research: freeze the checkpoint; predefine lag bands relative to the prediction target, removal counts, history-length strata, and hypotheses. Compare old, recent, and randomly selected interactions with equal per-user removal counts on the same eligible users; report exclusions and stratum sizes. Preserve chronological order, left padding, and final-nonpadding readout. Include unchanged-history controls and length-preserving replacements matched on observable item frequency, with repeated fixed random draws. Separately compare position-preserving replacement against deletion/repacking to detect positional effects. Replacement can introduce distribution shift; frozen ablations establish model sensitivity, while remove-and-retrain addresses a different question ([ROAR](https://research.google/pubs/evaluating-feature-importance-estimates/)).

Report baseline and ablated HR@10, paired differences in percentage points, and 95% paired-user bootstrap intervals: resample users jointly across conditions within each category, then recompute the four-category macro-average. Publish bootstrap settings, per-category/stratum results, and hit→miss/miss→hit counts; distinguish prespecified comparisons from exploratory searches and address multiplicity ([statistical-testing guidance](https://aclanthology.org/P18-1128/)). Keep validation users, targets, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed identical across conditions. Conclusions concern this sampled-candidate benchmark; sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog comparisons ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Training positive–negative margin changes, Δ[s(positive)−s(negative)], require identical sampled tuples and remain training-sensitivity diagnostics. Larger margins need not change top-10 membership or generalize. Evidence that older history harms this frozen model requires positive paired validation ΔHR@10 after old-history removal, uncertainty estimates, and improvement beyond matched-count random/recent controls across relevant length strata and replacement checks. This supports a model- and protocol-specific claim, not causal harm from older interactions or proof that retraining without them improves recommendations.
